purpose: Ask the ordinary chain the same question before wiring the historical route. B06, C03 and C02 each turned out to be a cascade, and reading source_mode selected the wrong level every time.

what_source_mode_says.why_that_is_not_the_answer: C02 carries the same source_mode and runs a deterministic extraction with zero model calls. The registry field describes the metric family, not which code answers it - this is the third time in this Issue that reading it as an implementation was wrong.

what_the_code_actually_does.dispatch: normal_run_v3 -> ordinary_remaining_cases (the else branch) -> its own D01 branch
what_the_code_actually_does.extraction: risk_signals.risk_factor_headings - pure regex over leading emphasis inside a located Item 1A; the module imports only re, typing, canonical and text_coverage
what_the_code_actually_does.so: D01 needs no model allowance. The earlier note in AGENTS.md that grouped it with B13/D03/D04 as 'blocked on model allowance' was wrong.

what_is_uniform.reading: one level, one shape, ten for ten - including the successor registrant, because D01 reads only its own target primary and never a prior period or a second filing. That is what makes it unlike B06 (seven levels, four Specs) and C02/C03 (two levels).

what_this_does_not_establish: what the ordinary chain ANSWERS for D01. This measured input preparation only; a route can prepare an input for every company and still resolve to RISK_HEADING_STRUCTURE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED for some of them.

that a pinned historical D01 reproduces those answers. The differential - ordinary versus historical, field for field - is owed before the route is called wired, the same as every other route in this Issue.
a_defect_in_this_probe_worth_recording: its optional second stage imported resolve_repository_file from vnext.records and raised ImportError for every company, which is why every row reads PROPOSAL_ERROR. The failure is the probe's, not the route's - the input layer above it succeeded. A reader who took the stage name at face value would have concluded the opposite of what was measured.

does_d01_hit_the_bound_that_stopped_pfiz.why_this_was_measured_before_wiring: D01's candidate builder enforces max_items exactly as D02's does, and that bound is what stopped Pfizer's D02 at 92 excerpts. A route that reports a Spec bound and a route that delivers a value are different things to put in the frame, and which one it is cannot be read off the code.
does_d01_hit_the_bound_that_stopped_pfiz.answer: no. Every company is under the bound: 28 to 60 headings, and the largest text is 10561 characters against 64000.

but_the_headroom_is_not_comfortable_and_.why_it_matters: the D02 lesson applies here unchanged - the item count depends on how the filer breaks up the section, not on how much is disclosed. Enphase is four headings from the bound with 10561 characters, a sixth of the character budget. A filer that splits its risk factors more finely would exceed max_items while using a fraction of max_text_chars, which is the same asymmetry D02 hit.
but_the_headroom_is_not_comfortable_and_.not_done: nothing is changed about the bound. This records where the route stands against it, not a proposal to move it.

one_company_is_blocked_for_another_reaso.jpmorgan_chase: 57 headings read here, but this probe goes through the ordinary current-source path. Historical period selection still refuses this company with SAVED_HISTORY_INCOHERENT, so a wired historical D01 would not reach the extractor for it. Counting it among the ten that 'fit' would overstate what a historical route delivers.

does_d01_hit_the_bound_that_stopped_pfiz.what_this_still_does_not_establish: that a pinned historical D01 reproduces these sets. The differential against the ordinary chain, field for field, is owed before the route is called wired - the same as every other route in this Issue.
